correctness.rationale: For k≥1 and θ_k(x)=xα(x)^k, semilattice grades obey γ(θ_k(x))=e∧f≤e. A strictly order-increasing grade rank h(e)=|{d:d≤e}|, plus θ permutation, forces e∧f=e for each x. Thus e≤f; since α is also a permutation, a second sum-of-ranks argument forces e=f, proving group-fibre rigidity. Every nilpotent maximal G splits P₂×Q_odd. For odd k, raising a Hall–Paige complete-map witness β on noncyclic P₂ to the inverse exponent ℓ (kℓ≡1 mod exp P₂) gives α_P; on odd Q choose a by CRT avoiding a=0 and 1+ka=0 mod each odd prime. If P₂ is cyclic nontrivial, product of the projected α,θ permutations in the cyclic Sylow factor would require unique involution z to satisfy z^k=1, impossible for odd k. This proves iff for all finite Clifford semigroups with nilpotent groups. Read verifier code for positive group factors and small exhaustive semilattices; finite samples do not establish universal fibre rigidity.
